judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied a successful WindowFrame-skin control, and a later comment supplies a single-instance workaround. Those discriminators should be tested rather than treating this as assigned or fixed by an older PotPlayer update.
evidence: Reported PowerToys 0.79.0 and PotPlayer 240315; the default window does not activate zones despite not being excluded.
The reporter says switching to WindowFrame makes it work.
A later user on PotPlayer 240509 reports closing all instances and starting one restores snapping.
Older #10221 was resolved by a 2021 PotPlayer update, not by a fix proven for this report.
judgment.recommended_action: Compare skin and instance-count controls and trace window eligibility before changing filtering.

fix_assessment.rationale: No linked implementation covers this report; a skin-dependent eligibility issue is plausible but not yet proven to be owned solely by PowerToys.

proposed_fixes.title: Recognize eligible skinned PotPlayer windows without accepting menus
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: PotPlayer skin or instance state changes the root/owner/style combination, causing FancyZones to reject a usable top-level window; the instance-count workaround may instead expose an independent app constraint.
plan: Capture DefineWindowType, owner/root and style values for default versus WindowFrame skins with one and multiple instances.
If PowerToys rejects a movable/resizable top-level window incorrectly, refine only the confirmed eligibility branch while preserving transient-window exclusions.
Add classifier tests for the captured style combinations and manual skin/instance regression scenarios; retain an external compatibility explanation if PotPlayer itself rejects resize.
verification: Default and WindowFrame skins both activate zones for eligible windows in the verified instance scenarios.
Menus, tooltips and non-resizable windows remain excluded; ordinary applications continue to snap.

confidence.rationale: Skin and instance controls support targeted classification testing, but actual HWND data and resize behavior have not been observed.

issue_context.summary: PotPlayer fails to engage FancyZones with its usual skin; WindowFrame works for the reporter, while another user reports a single-instance workaround.
known_information: The issue is open, unassigned and labeled app compatibility.
PowerToys was elevated and PotPlayer was not on the exclusion list.
Both useful workaround reports are already in the discussion and should not be requested again.
inferences: Skin-dependent window styles are a plausible discriminator.
Single-instance success is not proof that skin and instance symptoms share one root cause.
issue_context.analysis: A four-case maintainer test can distinguish style rejection from application-side resizing and prevent an unsafe broad filter relaxation.
initial_investigation: Read the full report and all three comments and checked the paginated timeline.
Read #10221: its author confirmed a PotPlayer update fixed a 2021 resize symptom; that does not close this later report.
Inspected FancyZonesWindowProcessing::DefineWindowType at main commit 3d6827a53a579ba9bedcf8d4bbda21348d78cbdb, including root, tool-window, popup, visible-owner and exclusion checks.
No PotPlayer installation or live resize test was performed.

actions.label: Compare PotPlayer skins and instance count

reproduce.title: Identify the PotPlayer window-classification discriminator
reproduce.version_requirement: Current supported builds; reported PotPlayer baselines are 240315 and 240509 with PowerToys 0.79.0.
prerequisites: A test PotPlayer installation with default and WindowFrame skins, a simple zone layout and no PotPlayer exclusion.
steps: 1. Close all PotPlayer instances and launch one using the default skin; Shift-drag into a zone.
3. Repeat both cases with multiple instances, restoring to one instance between controls.
4. Record each window's root/owner, styles, classifier return and whether direct resizing is accepted.
5. Validate any classifier correction against menus and ordinary resizable windows.
reproduce.expected_result: Eligible PotPlayer windows activate and fit zones; external resize constraints are recorded separately rather than bypassing all window checks.
